text.p: The $328,000 AT&T Challenge received its final decapitation on Thursday when Andre Agassi was bounced from the tournament by a 20-year old Swede.

Magnus Norman, ranked 81 and one of 10 Swedes in the top 100, ousted fourth-seeded Agassi, 7-6 (9-7) 3-6 6-3 in the second round. Agassi joined top-seeded Michael Chang, second seeded Jonas Bjorkman and third seeded Jim Courier on the sidelines, all of whom were eliminated earlier in the week.

Fifth seeded Petr Korda of the Czech Republic survived a three-set struggle with unseeded Johan Van Herck of Belgium, winning his second round match 6-4 1-6 6-3. Korda will play Norman in the quarterfinals.

Seventh-seeded Jason Stoltenberg of Australia also advanced with a 6-1 7-5 victory over Spain's Juan Albert Viloca. Stoltenberg will play Brazil's Fernando Meligeni in the quarterfinals. Meligeni beat Dennis van Scheppingen of the Netherlands, 6-3 7-6 (7-1.)
Agassi's match with Norman began as a protracted baseline struggle and ended in high drama as Norman appeared to have the match won, then saw it taken away by an umpire's over-rule.

Norman had missed his first match point at 5-3 in the third set but seemed to win it on the second match point when Agassi hit a forehand deep. But the umpire called the shot good as Norman protested. The Swede struggled to keep cool, fighting off a break point, then winning the match 6-3 on his third match point with a backhand winner up the line.

Agassi was challenged by the Swede from the start and fought off six set points against his serve in the first set before it went to the tiebreaker. Agassi let two set points of his own slip away in the tiebreaker before Norman won it 9-7 with a backhand volley winner.

Agassi appeared to take charge in the second set, breaking for a 3-1 lead and commanding the court with brilliant dropshots. But Norman broke back, then came close to taking a 4-3 lead as Agassi fought off break points. Instead, Agassi broke Norman for 5-3, then served out the set 6-3 when Norman netted a backhand.

Norman used his big serve and steady groundstrokes to stay even with Agassi in the third set, getting the only service break for a 5-3 lead as Agassi double-faulted, then missed a backhand. Norman served out the win in the next game. Norman had 18 aces in the match to Agassi's four.

"I knew I had to serve well and that's what I did today," said Norman, who was encouraged by having extended Agassi to three sets in their only previous match which Norman lost in February. Norman, who has kept a personal diary every day for two years since turning pro, said he read it again on Thursday morning to remind himself of his previous match with Agassi.
"I wrote in my diary I was too passive in that match," Norman said. "I read this this morning and I said to myself to go a little further inside the baseline."
Norman said he kept calm on the over-rule because "it was no big deal. I cannot get angry. I was playing Agassi and up 5-3. I won the match twice."

Agassi refused to speak to the media after the match and left the site immediately after the loss. He had suffered four consecutive first round losses this year before breaking through with two Davis Cup singles wins last month against the Netherlands.
